title: Cerebras Stock Surges After OpenAI CEO Calls Chipmaker a ‘Close Partner’
source_used: Investopedia text on its Yahoo Finance copy (same headline and time); Stocktwits text on Yahoo Finance for the reply context; Reuters market wrap (AOL copy) for the 9% close. Investopedia original not opened (HTTP 402).
key_facts: Cerebras shares rose on Monday 5 Oct 2026 (up 8% in recent trading, per Investopedia) after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called the company a 'close partner' in a social post; Reuters puts the gain at 9% at the close.
Altman said the companies have 'deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed'.

Stocktwits quotes the X post, made late Friday 2 Oct: 'There is some speculation about our partnership with Cerebras. Cerebras is a close partner, and we have a deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed.'

Cerebras shares had slumped about 20% the week before and closed Friday at $166.43, the lowest close since the May IPO, after research firm SemiAnalysis reported that OpenAI would use Nvidia GPUs rather than Cerebras hardware for the 'Ultrafast' mode of its GPT-6.1 Sol model.
A lockup expiry also added pressure: up to 19.4 million insider shares became eligible for sale on 30 Sep.
OpenAI is Cerebras' biggest customer by revenue backlog; the companies signed a $10 billion deal in January for 750 megawatts of computing power through 2028.
The stock is trading just below its $185 IPO price.
quote_evidence: Cerebras shares rose Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called the company a close partner.
Cerebras came under pressure after research firm SemiAnalysis reported that OpenAI would use Nvidia GPUs instead of Cerebras hardware for the "Ultrafast" mode of its GPT-6.1 Sol model.
Cerebras Systems rose 9% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on social media the chip designer is a "close partner" and that the companies have "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed."
why_it_matters_hint: A short public statement from OpenAI's chief executive lifted a stock that had fallen on doubts about the OpenAI deal, without saying which chips run the fast mode.
event_date: Altman's X post late Friday 2 Oct 2026; share rise Monday 5 Oct 2026
notes: REPLY STORY: Altman's post names no one; it is widely read (Stocktwits, Investopedia) as an answer to speculation after SemiAnalysis's claim, which we carried in our 1 Oct 2026 edition (OfficeChai).
